Your month of /MES and /MNQ day trades

Morgan, here is your October 2026.

You traded only /MES and /MNQ futures on 23 days, going both long and short in each. 42 of 53 trades ended the same day they were opened and 11 of 53 ended the day after, so nothing was left open at month end. 1 in 3 orders went in outside regular market hours, and with no rolls or adjustments, each trade was simply opened and then closed.

AT A GLANCE
- 53 trades: new trades you started
- the same day: how long you usually kept a trade
- $315 on /MNQ: your largest loss on a single trade
- 23 days: days you placed at least one trade

MANAGING
- You held or closed your trades without rolling any of them.

GETTING OUT
- You usually closed a trade the same day you opened it.

WHAT STOOD OUT
You switched direction within the same day. On Oct 1 you were both long and short /MNQ, and both trades ended with a loss. On Oct 20 you went long /MNQ twice and short once, and all three were closed at a loss the same day, alongside a short /MES you held to the next day.

Your /MNQ trades lost steadily before the first gain. Every /MNQ trade you opened from Oct 1 through Oct 14 ended with a loss, including $313 on Oct 13 and $307 and $295 on Oct 14. Your first /MNQ gain came on Oct 15, a short that closed up $346, your largest gain of the month.

Overnight holds were the exception, with mixed results. Only 11 of 53 trades were kept past the day they were opened. They ranged from a $209 gain on a short /MES opened Oct 5 to a $284 loss on a short /MNQ opened Oct 14.

HOW IT TURNED OUT
Your account ended the month down 15.1%, while the broad US market was up 0.7% and large technology companies were down 6.8%.
Of the 53 trades that ended, 17 ended with a gain and 36 with a loss.
Fees and commissions: $207.

WHAT CHANGED
New trades you opened: 26 in the first half of the month, 27 in the second half.

KO assigned, INTC closed and a SHOP roll

Drew, here is your October 2026.

Your month combined two positions carried over from August with two new ones. The KO covered call opened on Aug 10 was assigned on Oct 14, while the SHOP position from Aug 20 stayed open and became the one trade you rolled. On the new side, you paid a debit of $715 for an INTC long call on Oct 7, then bought F shares on Oct 22 and still held them at month end.

AT A GLANCE
- 2 trades: new trades you started
- 1 time: times you rolled a trade to a new strike or expiration
- none: share of your rolls done for a credit
- about 6 weeks: how far out the expiration usually was when you opened an options trade

GETTING IN
- You usually opened options trades expiring about 6 weeks out.
- You usually paid a debit of $143 per contract when you opened a trade.
- Implied volatility was usually average compared with its past year when you opened a trade.

MANAGING
- You rolled trades 1 time.
- None of your rolls were done for a credit.

GETTING OUT
- You usually kept a trade for about 6 weeks.
- When you closed an options trade, it was usually still 12 days from expiration.
- You closed 1 trade that ended with a loss before expiration.

WHAT STOOD OUT
Your losing trades ended in two different ways. KO was not closed by you; the covered call was assigned on Oct 14 after you had held it for about 2 months, for a loss of $601. INTC was the one you chose to exit: you closed the long call on Oct 27 with about 3 weeks left before expiration, for a loss of $251.

The second half of the month held most of the activity. After INTC opened on Oct 7, the later moves came close together: you bought F shares on Oct 22, rolled SHOP down to a lower strike and out to a later expiration on Oct 26, and closed INTC on Oct 27. SHOP and F were both still open at month end.

HOW IT TURNED OUT
Your account ended the month down 0.8%, while the broad US market was up 0.7% and large technology companies were down 6.8%.
Of the 2 trades that ended, 0 ended with a gain and 2 with a loss.
Fees and commissions: $8.74.

STILL OPEN
Going into next month: SHOP and F.

WHAT CHANGED
